definition: Learning statistical or neural models of musical structure — melody, harmony, rhythm — powering generation and analysis.
details: Learning statistical or neural models of musical structure — melody, harmony, rhythm — powering generation and analysis.

explainer.lead: Music modeling is learning statistical or neural models of musical structure — melody, harmony, rhythm — powering generation and analysis. It matters because such models underpin both creative tools and automated music understanding.

tiers.eli5: Learning the patterns of how tunes go, so you can predict what note or chord comes next.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers train models on symbolic or audio representations to predict the next event, then use them for generation or feature extraction. A pitfall is that long-range structure such as song form is hard to capture from short training windows.
tiers.paperLevel: Estimate a probability distribution over musical events (notes, chords, tokens) conditioned on prior context. Models capture local structure well but global form only weakly.

explainer.example: A model trained on melodies predicts likely next notes given the preceding bar and is used to suggest continuations.
